data.title: Some May Be Optimistic About Xero's (ASX:XRO) Earnings
data.description:
The market was pleased with the recent earnings report from Xero Limited (ASX:XRO), despite the profit numbers being soft. However, we think the company is showing some signs that things are more promising than they seem.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

A Closer Look At Xero's Earnings

As finance nerds would already know, the accrual ratio from cashflow is a key measure for assessing how well a company's free cash flow (FCF) matches its profit. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Xero recorded an accrual ratio of -0.12. That implies it has good cash conversion, and implies that its free cash flow solidly exceeded its profit last year. To wit, it produced free cash flow of NZ$426m during the period, dwarfing its reported profit of NZ$51.2m. Xero's free cash flow actually declined over the last year, which is disappointing, like non-biodegradable balloons.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Our Take On Xero's Profit Performance

Xero's accrual ratio is solid, and indicates strong free cash flow, as we discussed, above. Based on this observation, we consider it likely that Xero's statutory profit actually understates its earnings potential! On the other hand, its EPS actually shrunk in the last twelve months.   • The build out of Dell Technologies' AI Data Platform, direct liquid cooled Exascale storage and validated NVIDIA AI environments points to a push toward higher value infrastructure and services around a US$95b AI backlog and more than US$130b of AI server orders over the past 12 months.

Dell Technologies Investment Narrative Recap

To own Dell Technologies, you need to believe the firm can turn its very large AI infrastructure order book into higher quality earnings, not just more hardware volume. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St leans on accelerating AI server demand, a US$95b backlog and US$74b of guided AI server revenue to support that view. The biggest near term catalyst remains how quickly that backlog converts into shipped systems and cash, especially with recent share price weakness sharpening attention on execution.

The main risk is that AI servers stay low margin while traditional PCs and legacy hardware remain under pricing pressure. Management already faces tight supply across key components, and that could slow backlog conversion or squeeze margins if costs rise faster than selling prices. The expanded AI Factory news does not remove those issues, and it also pushes more of Dell Technologies' mix toward storage, software and services that can offset some rate dilution if customers adopt the broader stack at scale.

The most relevant update is the expansion of the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA, including the AI Data Platform, direct liquid cooled Exascale storage and large scale infrastructure management software. This directly touches the core thesis that Dell Technologies can move up the stack from selling AI servers to running more of the AI data center, which ties into the large order pipeline already in place.

Operationally, this matters because growth in AI servers is currently rate dilutive and relies on attaching higher margin storage and services to lift overall profitability. The new liquid cooled storage, OpenManage Rack Scale and Fabric Manager give Dell Technologies more ways to sell that fuller configuration into big GPU environments. For the next few quarters, investors will likely watch whether reported ISG margins and storage contribution move in step with the US$130b plus of AI orders described in the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St.

Dell Technologies AI Factory Through the Analyst Lens

Dell Technologies' narrative projects US$266.7b revenue and US$20.8b earnings by 2029. This rests on 20.8% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$9.4b from US$11.4b today.

Analysts effectively tie the expanded AI Factory push to a broader financial story for Dell Technologies. The consensus view assumes that earnings move from US$11.4b today to US$20.8b by 2029, while revenue compounds at 20.8% a year and margins edge from 7.5% to 7.8%. That path implies the business leans heavily on AI infrastructure demand. That brings two moving parts for readers to test. The first is whether the firm can actually get to those profit levels given hardware margin pressures. The second is whether the market would be comfortable assigning a lower multiple to that earnings stream while AI infrastructure themes remain central to the story.

There is also a clear link between these forecasts and capital return expectations. Analysts are baking in a 4.06% yearly decline in shares outstanding over the next three years. Fewer shares can amplify earnings per share if net income meets the projected US$20.8b level, which partly explains why consensus is comfortable with a P/E that is lower than both today’s multiple and the sector reference. For investors watching the AI Factory expansion, the key question is whether cash generation from AI servers, storage and services can keep funding those buybacks alongside data center build outs without stretching the balance sheet.

Price targets round out this picture. The current analyst consensus sits at US$594.16, only 3.7% above the US$572.47 share price referenced in the report, with a wide band between US$480.0 and US$735.0. That narrow gap between current price and target suggests the average view is that Dell Technologies already reflects a bullish interpretation of its AI infrastructure opportunity. data.title: What Xiaomi Bears Saw Before The Fall
data.description:
If you had looked at Xiaomi on 1 January 2026 and decided to sit it out, the move might feel easier to justify now. For Xiaomi shareholders, the loss from the start of the year was 29.2%, including dividends. That decline came alongside rising memory costs, heavier EV losses, and softer smartphone demand reported later in the period. The real question is which early assumptions about margins, capital intensity, or market maturity were already on record before any of that news arrived.

Narratives are how investors here put a case on the record, with explicit assumptions about revenue, margins and the multiple. Those assumptions imply an estimated Fair Value.

Xiaomi is not the only name tied to this theme. Zero in on 33 elite gold producer stocks and compare how each one is priced.

The Two Xiaomi Stories Investors Had To Weigh

The shares cost HK$39.3 at the start of the period, and anyone considering Xiaomi then had to choose between two sharply different expectations for where the business might be headed.

The bullish narrative saw a Fair Value of HK$66.01, or 68% above the start price. It leaned on Xiaomi pushing deeper into premium smartphones, appliances, and EVs, with analysts assuming 21.3% revenue growth and a 9.1% profit margin over a 3 year horizon.

The bearish case put Fair Value at HK$35.12, or 11% below the start price. That view focused on smartphone saturation and heavier research spending, with analysts in that camp assuming 16.5% revenue growth and a profit margin drifting to 7.6% over roughly the same period.

What The Results Changed For The Xiaomi Thesis

Xiaomi’s later report showed Q2 2026 revenue at C¥108,921.609m and net income at C¥9,462.405m, both below Q2 2025, with net margin sliding from 10.3% to 8.7%. That outcome leaned toward the cautious case on profitability. News of rising memory costs, EV losses and a profit slump reinforced that pressure, so the period cut both ways for the original narratives.

The lesson is simple. When a story leans on margin expansion, track the reported net margin and segment level cost lines rather than only top line growth or product launches.

What Xiaomi's Drop Leaves You Paying For Today

Xiaomi now trades at HK$28.52, with this Narrative's Fair Value sitting above that level. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St frames that gap around Xiaomi's ability to use its Mobile × AIoT ecosystem and premium hardware to reshape its mix.

A buyer today would be assuming heavy AI, EV and R&D spending ultimately turns into durable monetisation across devices, software and higher margin internet services rather than staying mostly a cost line.
